stories.title: Design Firm Twelve Doubles HQ at Two Trees’ 45 Main Street to 14K SF
stories.excerpt: Design firm Twelve has upped its Brooklyn office headquarters by twofold. Twelve inked a 7,000-square-foot lease expansion at Dumbo’s 45 Main Street, according to a spokesperson for landlord Two Trees Management. The deal doubles Twelve’s office footprint to 14,000 square feet, spanning part of the 12-story office building’s sixth floor. The seven-year lease carried an asking rent of $52 per square foot. Crain’s New York first reported on the deal. Twelve, founded in 2005, produces merchandise and packaging for brands, and names Dior and the New York Times among its clients. In addition to its Dumbo base, the firm maintains global offices in Paris, London, Hong Kong and Shenzhen. Twelve did not work with a broker on the expansion. Two Trees was represented in-house by Alyssa Zahler and Elizabeth Bueno. “Twelve’s decision to double its footprint in Dumbo is a testament to the enduring appeal of the neighborhood as a home for creative businesses,” Bueno said in a statement. Prior to its decade-plus tenure at 45 Main Street, Twelve spent three years at Two Trees’ 55 Washington Street, located just around the corner. The firm arrived at Main Street in 2015 and increased its footprint there multiple times, according to Two Trees. Twelve’s move into another 7,000 square feet is expected to take place in the first quarter of 2027. “Doubling our space gives our incredible team more room to collaborate and spread their wings,” Katie Conovitz, founder and CEO of Twelve, said in a statement. “Equally important, the expansion allows us to continue hosting our incredible clients, with the ambition that each one leaves feeling inspired and energized.” The 476,000-square-foot office building on Main Street between Front and Water streets hosts a roster of design studios and other creative firms, including recent arrivals Church Edit, a film editing services collective, and Think! bullets: Design firm Twelve doubles HQ at Two Trees' 45 Main Street, Dumbo to 14K SF
7-year lease expansion at $52/SF signals creative tenant confidence in Brooklyn office
Firm doubles footprint after decade-plus tenure; maintaining global offices in Paris, London, Asia
stories.summary: Design firm Twelve has expanded its headquarters at Two Trees Management's 45 Main Street in Dumbo by 7,000 SF, doubling its footprint to 14,000 SF on a seven-year lease at $52/SF. The company, which produces merchandise and packaging for major brands including Dior and The New York Times, has maintained a presence at the property for over a decade. Two Trees stated the expansion reflects Dumbo's continued appeal as a home for creative businesses.
stories.impact: Creative office tenants anchoring in Dumbo signals sustained demand for high-end, design-forward office space in Brooklyn. This renewal and expansion—despite broader office headwinds—suggests that trophy trophy office corridors near waterfront amenities in NYC still command pricing power and attract growing firms; developers should monitor Dumbo's creative-class retention as a leading indicator for Brooklyn office recovery and mixed-use development potential.

stories.title: AT&T Renews 7K-SF Lease at Rudin’s 3 Times Square
stories.excerpt: Home is where the heart is, and telecommunications giant at&t is quite at home in the heart of Times Square. The wireless carrier has renewed and extended its lease at Rudin’s 3 Times Square for another five years, Commercial Observer has learned. AT&T occupies 6,623 square feet of ground-floor and lower-level retail space at the 925,000-square-foot Midtown office tower. AT&T moved into the 30-story property, located on Seventh Avenue between West 42nd and West 43rd streets, in 2008. “Times Square remains one of the world’s most dynamic and heavily trafficked retail corridors in the world, and AT&T’s renewed commitment at 3 Times Square reinforces its spot at the center of it all,” Kevin Daly, vice president of commercial leasing at Rudin, said in a statement. Daly represented Rudin in-house alongside Craig Panzirer, senior vice president and head of office leasing at Rudin. The asking rent for the AT&T deal was not disclosed. The average asking rent for retail space in Times Square was $1,400 per square foot during the third quarter of 2026, according to CBRE data. The tenant was represented by Loren Baron from CBRE. Baron did not immediately respond to CO’s request for comment. “Extending our lease at 3 Times Square reflects AT&T’s long-term commitment to New York City and to serving customers in one of the world’s most vibrant commercial districts,” Keron Incarnato, AT&T’s vice president and general manager for the Northeast, said in a statement. “This location keeps us connected to the people, businesses and visitors who power the city, while giving customers a convenient place to explore the latest devices, services and connectivity solutions.” The AT&T extension follows Rudin’s April 2026 retail lease with jeweler Pandora, which took 4,107 square feet at 3 Times Square, CO reported in the spring. bullets: AT&T renews 6,623 SF retail lease at Rudin's 3 Times Square for five years
Tenant occupying ground and lower-level retail since 2008; lease terms not disclosed
Flagship Times Square retail corridor remains anchored by major national carrier through 2030
stories.summary: AT&T has renewed and extended its lease at Rudin's 3 Times Square for another five years, occupying 6,623 SF of ground-floor and lower-level retail space in the 925,000 SF Midtown office tower. The carrier has been a tenant since 2008. Kevin Daly of Rudin noted that Times Square remains one of the world's most heavily trafficked retail corridors, reinforcing AT&T's commitment to the location.
stories.impact: AT&T's 5-year renewal without disclosed rate concessions indicates that marquee national retailers view Times Square ground-floor retail as essential flagship territory despite soft office fundamentals. This signals strong retail demand independent of office weakness; developers should view Times Square as a mixed-use anchor opportunity with resilient retail rents and foot traffic insulated from office vacancies.

stories.title: Kam Sang Acquires Loan on DTLA’s Wells Fargo Center South at Discount
stories.excerpt: Newmark completed the discounted sale of the $290-million loan collateralized by the fee simple interest in Wells Fargo Center South, a Class A office tower at 355 S. Grand in Downtown Los Angeles’ Bunker Hill district. The loan was acquired by New Age 355, LLC, an affiliate of Kam Sang Company, Inc. Newmark co-head, U.S. Capital Markets Kevin Shannon and vice chairmen Ken White, Laura Stumm, Rob Hannan and Michael Moll represented the undisclosed seller. Designed by Skidmore, Owings & Merrill, the property encompasses approximately 1.16 million square feet across 45 stories. At the time of the loan sale, the property was approximately 42% leased. “This transaction reflects the growing pool of investors and owner-users seeking opportunities in institutional-quality assets across Downtown Los Angeles,” said Shannon. “As pricing continues to adjust, buyers are gaining access to irreplaceable real estate at a compelling basis relative to replacement cost. We are seeing increasing conviction from groups that recognize the long-term value of premier office properties and are willing to invest in their next chapter.” The post Kam Sang Acquires Loan on DTLA’s Wells Fargo Center South at Discount appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Kam Sang acquires $290M loan on Wells Fargo Center South, DTLA at discounted price
Class A office tower 1.16M SF, 45 stories, 42% leased; SOM-designed Bunker Hill asset

stories.summary: Kam Sang Company acquired the $290 million loan collateralized by Wells Fargo Center South, a 1.16 million SF, 45-story Class A office tower at 355 S. Grand in Downtown LA's Bunker Hill district, at a discounted price via Newmark. At the time of sale, the property was 42% leased. Kevin Shannon of Newmark noted the transaction reflects growing investor appetite for institutional-quality assets as pricing adjusts relative to replacement cost.
stories.impact: Distressed office loan sales in premium DTLA markets signal cap rate expansion and valuation reset; however, Kam Sang's acquisition on value thesis suggests selective institutional capital sees long-term upside in trophy properties with low basis. Multifamily developers should monitor DTLA's office distress as a proxy for broader CRE credit stress and potential for land/asset recycling into alternative uses (conversion, mixed-use) as office recovery stalls.

stories.title: Brooklyn Powerhouse Sports to Open 11K-SF Facility in Sunset Park
stories.excerpt: Brooklyn Powerhouse Sports, a new fitness and athletic training facility, is opening its first location. Brooklyn Powerhouse has signed a 10,871-square-foot lease at Capstone Equities’ 14 53rd Street, known as the Whale Building, near the shore of New York Harbor in Sunset Park, Commercial Observer has learned. The company will set up batting cages and a small office at the location. The tenant will occupy space on the property’s third floor for eight years, at an asking rent of $28 per square foot, according to landlord broker Newmark. “This lease continues the transformation of the Whale Building into a destination for experiential and active tenants, joining Soccer Roof and the strong wave of leasing we’ve completed at the property,” Edward Kent of Capstone Equities said in a statement. “We’re excited to bring a new sports and entertainment offering to Sunset Park and the broader Brooklyn community.” Bernard Weitzman, Ryan Gessin, Jordan Gosin and Rohan Kapur from Newmark represented the landlord in this deal. The brokers declined to comment. Brooklyn Powerhouse’s new Sunset Park facility will feature dedicated spaces for baseball and softball training, including batting cages and tech simulators. “Opening Brooklyn Powerhouse Sports has been a dream of ours, and we’re proud to bring Brooklyn its premier batting cage facility,” Shamus Connolly, founder of Brooklyn Powerhouse Sports, said in a statement. “We’ve designed this space for players of all abilities — from kids taking their first swings to seasoned athletes working on their mechanics. We can’t wait to welcome the community.” The tenant was represented by Whitten Morris from JLL. “Brooklyn Powerhouse Sports had a very specific vision for its first facility, so finding the right space was especially important,” Morris said. “The property at 14 53rd Street offered the size and flexibility needed to bring that vision to life, while providing a strong foundation for the business a
bullets: Brooklyn Powerhouse Sports signs 10,871 SF lease at Capstone Equities' Whale Building, Sunset Park
8-year lease at $28/SF; sports/athletic facility with batting cages opening first location
Experiential tenant joins Soccer Roof; signals active use-case diversification in industrial-adjacent Sunset Park
stories.summary: Brooklyn Powerhouse Sports, a new fitness and athletic training facility, has signed a 10,871 SF lease on the third floor of Capstone Equities' 14 53rd Street (the Whale Building) in Sunset Park for eight years at $28/SF. The facility will feature batting cages and office space. Capstone noted the lease continues the Whale Building's transformation into a destination for experiential and active tenants, alongside existing tenant Soccer Roof.
stories.impact: Experiential, active-use tenants clustering in Sunset Park's industrial-waterfront corridor signals demand for mixed-use repurposing of older flex/industrial buildings. This demand—coupled with lower rents ($28/SF) and large floor plates—creates conversion and repositioning opportunities for multifamily developers; Sunset Park's supply of large, flexible spaces near transit and waterfront may attract adaptive-use or mixed-use development combining residential, retail, and entertainment.

stories.title: Northmarq Arranges $19M Sale of Kent Canyon Ridge Plaza in WA
stories.excerpt: Northmarq’s Pacific Northwest Investment Sales team, led by Sean Tufts, Kevin Adatto, Joe Dugoni, and Jack Hallberg, completed the $19 million sale of Canyon Ridge Plaza, an 86,909-square-foot multi-tenant retail community center located at 26015 104th Ave. SE in Kent, Washington. The property was acquired by Kimco Realty. “Shopping centers continue to be one of the most sought-after asset classes in commercial real estate, with institutional capital committing to the space despite a challenging market environment,” said Tufts. “Centers with a strong off-price and value roster remain at the top of that demand.” Canyon Ridge Plaza is shadow-anchored by a corporate-owned Target, with a tenant roster that includes Ross Dress for Less, Old Navy, Petco, Bath & Body Works and Verizon Wireless. The property is 94% leased. Six tenants have executed new or extended long-term leases since January 2025, including a 10-year renewal from Ross Dress for Less. Burlington, TJ Maxx and Harbor Freight have recently opened adjacent to the center. The post Northmarq Arranges $19M Sale of Kent Canyon Ridge Plaza in WA appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Kimco Realty acquires Canyon Ridge Plaza, Kent WA for $19M; 86,909 SF retail center
94% leased; shadow-anchored by corporate Target; tenants include Ross, Old Navy, Petco
Six tenants signed new/extended long-term leases since Jan 2025; off-price/value format outperforming
stories.summary: Northmarq completed the $19 million sale of Canyon Ridge Plaza, an 86,909 SF multi-tenant retail center in Kent, Washington, to Kimco Realty. The property is shadow-anchored by a corporate-owned Target and 94% leased with tenants including Ross Dress for Less, Old Navy, Petco, Bath & Body Works, and Verizon Wireless. Six tenants have signed new or extended long-term leases since January 2025, including a 10-year renewal from Ross.
stories.impact: Off-price and value-driven retail (Ross, TJ Maxx, Target) remains resilient, with institutional capital (Kimco) actively acquiring stabilized shopping centers in suburban Pacific Northwest markets. This signals strong demand fundamentals for convenience/value retail anchored by national brands; multifamily developers in Seattle-Tacoma suburbs should expect continued retail competition for land and note that strong retail demand may support mixed-use residential-retail development in similar infill locations.

stories.title: Stephen Ross Buys Second Boca Raton Office Property for $64M
stories.excerpt: Stephen Ross’s office shopping spree continues in Boca Raton, Fla. The billionaire’s firm, Related Ross, paid $64 million for North 40, a 380,823-square-foot office complex. The two-building property at 5201 Congress Avenue is adjacent West Yamato Road and west of Interstate 95, about a mile from a Tri-Rail station. The office complex, which was built in 1984, is 74 percent occupied. The sellers, Mainstreet Capital Partners and Partners Group, renovated the 23-acre asset, adding a shared kitchen, a bar, conference rooms and a fitness center. It’s unclear when, or for how much, the joint venture acquired the property. JLL‘s Hermen Rodriguez, Matt McCormack and Ike Ojala represented the sellers in the recent transaction. The purchase comes about two months after Related Ross paid an undisclosed amount to buy the 124-acre BRiC office campus, which is less than a mile from North 40. “Together, these two properties create an opportunity to invest in a connected and thoughtfully planned destination in one of South Florida’s most strategic locations with direct access to I-95, the Tri-Rail, and Florida Atlantic University,” Jordan Bargas, executive vice president at Related Ross, said in a statement. The Marcel Breuer-designed property houses 1.7 million square feet of office space and is where IBM designed the first personal computer in the 1960s. The developer plans to add retail space and housing. The acquisitions are part of Stephen Ross’s plan to turn Palm Beach County into a leading business hub. He started in West Palm Beach, where he has become the biggest owner of Class A office buildings. Two office developments are under construction after securing $772 million in financing. The billionaire has also donated millions for Vanderbilt University to open a $520 million campus and for private grade schools to expand to West Palm Beach. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Stephen Ross (Related) acquires North 40 office complex, Boca Raton FL for $64M
380,823 SF, two-building property; 74% occupied; built 1984, recently renovated
Related Ross buying second Boca Raton office asset in two months; 1 mile from Tri-Rail station
stories.summary: Related Ross, the commercial real estate firm of billionaire Stephen Ross, paid $64 million for North 40, a 380,823 SF office complex comprising two buildings at 5201 Congress Avenue in Boca Raton, Florida. The property, built in 1984 and recently renovated, is 74% occupied and located adjacent to West Yamato Road and west of I-95, approximately one mile from a Tri-Rail station. This purchase follows Related Ross's acquisition of the 124-acre BRiC office campus less than a mile away about two months prior.
stories.impact: Related Ross's rapid, sequential acquisition of two large office campuses in Boca Raton—positioning them as interconnected destinations near transit—signals a strategic bet on South Florida office consolidation and potential repositioning. High-profile developer aggregation of office assets suggests future conversion/mixed-use redevelopment potential; multifamily developers should track Boca Raton's office recovery timeline and Related's repositioning strategy as an indicator of demand for residential/hospitality/mixed-use alternatives to legacy office.

stories.title: Somerville Apartment Portfolio Sale Sets Pricing Benchmark
stories.excerpt: Matthews represented the seller in the disposition of the Kingsley Orchard Realty Portfolio, located at 18 Day St., 49 Dover St. and 123 Orchard St. in Somerville, MA. VP Nick Jasinski facilitated the $39,000,000 transaction, reportedly the largest multifamily portfolio sale in the Davis Square submarket within the past 15 years. The buyer was not disclosed. The 120-unit portfolio comprises three brick apartment buildings located within one block of each other in Somerville’s Davis Square neighborhood. After developing and holding the three properties for more than a century, Kingsley Orchard Realty Limited Partnership brought the portfolio to market for the first time. “Opportunities of this scale with more than a century of continuous family ownership are increasingly rare in Greater Boston,” Jasinski said. “Our priority was to maximize exposure, create competition, and deliver the strongest possible outcome for the family while keeping the transaction on schedule.” The post Somerville Apartment Portfolio Sale Sets Pricing Benchmark appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Kingsley Orchard Realty Portfolio sells for $39M in Somerville's Davis Square, MA
120-unit portfolio across three brick buildings; largest Davis Square multifamily sale in 15 years
First disposition after century-plus family ownership; buyer undisclosed; portfolio fully leased
stories.summary: Matthews represented the sale of the Kingsley Orchard Realty Portfolio comprising three brick apartment buildings (18 Day St., 49 Dover St., and 123 Orchard St.) in Somerville's Davis Square for $39 million. The 120-unit portfolio, developed and held by the family for over a century, sold for the first time. The transaction is reportedly the largest multifamily portfolio sale in the Davis Square submarket within the past 15 years.
stories.impact: First-time portfolio sale of century-old family multifamily in Boston's Davis Square at $39M sets pricing benchmark for core Boston residential in transitional urban submarkets; loss of long-term hold suggests family capital exiting or consolidating. Multifamily developers should view this as a market signal that Davis Square values have reached levels attractive to institutional capital and may see accelerated portfolio consolidation; similar aging family properties nearby may now enter market, creating acquisition windows in walkable, transit-accessible Boston submarkets.

stories.title: PRC Acquires Downtown Richmond Apartments, Plans Seniors Housing
stories.excerpt: People Restoring Communities (PRC), an affordable housing development firm, announced the acquisition of Grace Street Apartments, an 11-story residential building located at 400 East Grace Street in downtown Richmond, Virginia. PRC, in a joint venture with The Delaine Companies and in partnership with the Richmond Redevelopment & Housing Authority (RRHA), plans to substantially rehabilitate the long-vacant property and create 68 affordable apartments for seniors. PRC acquired the property through a ground lease with an upfront payment of approximately $4.9 million. The acquisition was financed with a $3.3 million bridge loan from Low Income Investment Fund, with PRC contributing approximately $1.6 million in equity, both of which are expected to be repaid with funds available at the project’s construction closing. The planned rehabilitation will reconfigure the building’s existing 58 apartments, which are currently a mix of studios, one-, and two-bedroom apartments, into 68 homes tailored to low-income seniors, while upgrading the building’s ground-floor commercial space. The rehabilitation is expected to begin in the Spring of 2027 and be completed by the end of 2028. The post PRC Acquires Downtown Richmond Apartments, Plans Seniors Housing appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: PRC acquires Grace Street Apartments, downtown Richmond VA; ground lease $4.9M upfront

stories.summary: People Restoring Communities (PRC), in joint venture with The Delaine Companies and partnering with Richmond Redevelopment & Housing Authority, acquired Grace Street Apartments, an 11-story residential building in downtown Richmond, Virginia, via ground lease for approximately $4.9 million upfront. PRC plans to substantially rehabilitate the long-vacant property and create 68 affordable apartments for seniors, reconfiguring existing 58 units and upgrading ground-floor commercial space. The project is financed with a $3.3 million bridge loan from Low Income Investment Fund and $1.6 million equity; rehabilitation is scheduled spring 2027 through end 2028.
stories.impact: Long-vacant downtown Richmond multifamily repositioning into senior affordable housing via mission-driven developer with gap financing signals strong policy/philanthropic support for adaptive reuse and elderly housing in secondary markets. This deal flags emerging demand for senior housing nationally and potential for multifamily developers to acquire distressed urban properties at favorable basis for conversion to age-restricted or affordable housing with HUD/LIHTC subsidy stacking.

stories.title: St. John Properties Signs Inaugural Five Leases at Hunt Valley Exchange
stories.excerpt: St. John Properties, Inc. has signed five inaugural leases at Hunt Valley Exchange totaling more than 26,000 square feet. The 110,000 square foot mixed-use community at the corner of York Road and Wight Avenue includes two 23,000 square foot flex and R&D buildings at 25 and 35 Wight Avenue, and an 8,165 square foot inline retail building at 11060 York Road. Dunkin’, Elite Golf Studios, GPT Wine & Spirits, and Spicy Olive Indian Restaurant have signed leases and are expected to open by year-end, with The Goddard School scheduled to follow in 2027. St. John Properties acquired the 17-acre site in 2023 and has since delivered the speculative space, flex, R&D, and retail space. The project is now 67% leased, with approximately 30,000 square feet of space remaining, while the company continues to market two retail pad sites for future development. The buildings feature all-brick-and-glass exteriors, 18-foot ceiling heights, and rear dock and drive-in loading. The post St. John Properties Signs Inaugural Five Leases at Hunt Valley Exchange appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: St. John Properties signs five inaugural leases at Hunt Valley Exchange, Baltimore totaling 26K SF

stories.summary: St. John Properties signed five inaugural leases at Hunt Valley Exchange, a 110,000 SF mixed-use community at York Road and Wight Avenue in Baltimore, totaling more than 26,000 SF. Tenants include Dunkin', Elite Golf Studios, GPT Wine & Spirits, Spicy Olive Indian Restaurant (opening by year-end), and The Goddard School (2027). The property comprises two 23,000 SF flex/R&D buildings and an 8,165 SF inline retail building and is now 67% leased with ~30,000 SF and two retail pad sites remaining.
stories.impact: Speculative mixed-use development achieving 67% preleasing with strong operational/retail anchors signals healthy demand for flex/R&D and experiential retail in suburban Baltimore. St. John's active leasing velocity and pad-site strategy indicate that Baltimore's secondary office/R&D corridor (Hunt Valley) remains attractive for amenity-rich mixed-use; multifamily developers should view this as validation of market appetite for mixed-use densification in suburban employment nodes.

stories.title: Life Sciences Vacancy Near 27% for Three Biggest U.S. Hubs
stories.excerpt: The nation’s largest life sciences hubs are still struggling with elevated real estate vacancy rates and a slowdown in venture capital funding. Despite some pharmaceutical companies making big leasing commitments, Greater Boston, the San Francisco Bay Area and San Diego County have vacancies ranging from nearly 24 percent to more than 28 percent after the third quarter of 2026, according to new reports from Savills. The three markets also recorded annual declines in venture capital funding during the quarter. Greater Boston, the largest of the three life sciences markets by inventory with 44.4 million square feet, is being weighed down by oversupply. Overall vacancy reached 28.1 percent during the third quarter, while another 3.2 million square feet is under construction. The region’s venture capital funding totaled $2.7 billion during the third quarter, down from $3.2 billion a year earlier. Meanwhile, National Institutes of Health funding declined by about $200 million from 2025, although the Boston area continued to attract more NIH funding than either the Bay Area or San Diego. Some pharmaceutical companies expanded their footprints in Greater Boston in the third quarter. Sanofi accounted for two of the market’s largest leases, covering 500,000 square feet at 350 Water Street and another 400,000 square feet at 450 Water Street in Cambridge. Roche‘s Genentech also opened a 95,000-square-foot center at Harvard‘s Enterprise Research Campus in Boston’s Allston neighborhood with a 10-year lease. Also, Gillette acquired 232 A Street in Boston’s Seaport District for $99.3 million. The 325,000-square-foot development site is planned to become the company’s headquarters. Meanwhile, the San Francisco Bay Area posted a 23.8 percent vacancy rate in its life sciences space during the third quarter, down 20 basis points from a year earlier. The market’s life sciences inventory grew slightly to 37.2 million square feet. Venture capital
bullets: Greater Boston, San Francisco, San Diego life sciences vacancy 24–28%; Q3 2026 data from Savills
Greater Boston 28.1% vacant, 3.2M SF under construction, $2.7B VC funding (down from $3.2B YoY)
NIH funding declined ~$200M from 2025; pharma leasing commitments insufficient to absorb oversupply
stories.summary: The three largest U.S. life sciences hubs—Greater Boston, San Francisco Bay Area, and San Diego County—are experiencing elevated real estate vacancy and weakened venture capital funding. Greater Boston, the largest hub with 44.4 million SF, recorded 28.1% vacancy in Q3 2026, with an additional 3.2 million SF under construction. VC funding in Greater Boston totaled $2.7 billion in Q3 2026, down from $3.2 billion a year earlier. National Institutes of Health funding also declined approximately $200 million from 2025.
stories.impact: Life sciences oversupply in top three markets—despite marquee pharma leasing—signals structural demand weakness and potential long-term real estate surplus; Greater Boston's 3.2M SF pipeline amid 28% vacancy is a severe warning. Multifamily developers should avoid overbuilding near life sciences parks until VC and NIH funding stabilize; conversely, this presents a window to acquire distressed life sciences real estate at discount for conversion to residential, lab-to-loft, or alternative mixed-use in innovation-adjacent neighborhoods.
